plan: This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), bidding exactly my value of $25 ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value exceeds the price I'd pay) and never overpay. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if the second-highest bid exceeds $25, while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, the optimal strategy is to bid my true value of $25.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Bidding exactly my value ($18) ensures I never pay more than the item is worth to me, and I maximize my expected profit since overbidding risks paying more than my value, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With no other information about opponents' strategies, truthful bidding is optimal.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the weakly dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), so bidding above my value only risks paying more than the item is worth if I end up setting the price myself relative to others. Bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. With no prior round history to adjust from, I'll bid my true value of $31.
